info.brief: Shared settings and math helpers for the Operator camera controller. The camera itself
info.description:
Shared settings and math helpers for the Operator camera controller. The camera itself
is driven by the properties and messages of `operator/operator/operator.script`
(`activate`, `follow_point`, `manual_control` and the rest), which are not members of
this module. The settings fields are plain module fields; assigning one goes through a
cast, since a namespace import is read-only:
`(operator as { flight_look_easing: (this: void, x: number) => number }).flight_look_easing = (x) => x`.

elements.name: lerp
elements.brief: Linearly interpolates from `a` to `b`, returning `a + (b - a) * t`. `t` is not
elements.description:
Linearly interpolates from `a` to `b`, returning `a + (b - a) * t`. `t` is not
clamped, so a value outside `0` to `1` extrapolates.

elements.name: lerp
elements.brief: Linearly interpolates from vector `a` to vector `b`, returning `a + (b - a) * t` as a
elements.description:
Linearly interpolates from vector `a` to vector `b`, returning `a + (b - a) * t` as a
new vector. `t` is not clamped, so a value outside `0` to `1` extrapolates.

elements.name: angle_between
elements.brief: Returns the angle between two vectors, in degrees from `0` to `180`. A vector of zero
elements.description:
Returns the angle between two vectors, in degrees from `0` to `180`. A vector of zero
length gives NaN.

elements.name: project_on_plane
elements.brief: Projects a vector onto the plane through the origin with the given normal, returning
elements.description:
Projects a vector onto the plane through the origin with the given normal, returning
`v - plane_normal * vmath.dot(plane_normal, v)`. The normal must have unit length for
the result to lie on the plane.

parameters.name: plane_normal
parameters.doc: The plane's normal, of unit length.

elements.name: quat_from_euler
elements.brief: Converts Euler angles in degrees to a rotation, composed as `z * y * x` from the
elements.description:
Converts Euler angles in degrees to a rotation, composed as `z * y * x` from the
rotations about each axis.

parameters.name: euler
parameters.doc: The angles about the `x`, `y` and `z` axes, in degrees.

elements.name: euler_from_quat
elements.brief: Converts a rotation to Euler angles in degrees, about the `x`, `y` and `z` axes. It
elements.description:
Converts a rotation to Euler angles in degrees, about the `x`, `y` and `z` axes. It
reads them back in the order `y * x * z`, so it reverses `quat_from_euler` when the
`z` angle is `0`. At an `x` angle near 90 or -90 degrees the `z` angle is `0`.

elements.name: normalized_target_angle
elements.brief: Returns `target`, shifted by one full turn when that makes the turn from `original`
elements.description:
Returns `target`, shifted by one full turn when that makes the turn from `original`
no more than 180 degrees, so an animation from `original` takes the short way round.

elements.name: normalized_target_euler
elements.brief: Applies `normalized_target_angle` to each of the `x`, `y` and `z` angles, returning a
elements.description:
Applies `normalized_target_angle` to each of the `x`, `y` and `z` angles, returning a
new vector.

parameters.name: original
parameters.doc: The current Euler angles, in degrees.

parameters.name: target
parameters.doc: The wanted Euler angles, in degrees.

elements.name: clamp_angle
elements.brief: Brings an angle beyond 360 or -360 degrees back by one full turn, then clamps it
elements.description:
Brings an angle beyond 360 or -360 degrees back by one full turn, then clamps it
between `min` and `max`.

parameters.name: min
parameters.doc: The smallest angle returned, in degrees.

parameters.name: max
parameters.doc: The largest angle returned, in degrees.

elements.name: camera_collisions_groups
elements.brief: The collision groups tested by the raycast from the operator anchor to the camera, so
elements.description:
The collision groups tested by the raycast from the operator anchor to the camera, so
the camera stays in front of obstacles. Read on every raycast. Starts as
`[hash("default")]`.

elements.name: flight_bezier_samples_count
elements.brief: The number of bezier segments an operator samples a flight path with, which sets how
elements.description:
The number of bezier segments an operator samples a flight path with, which sets how
accurate its uniform position is. Read each time an operator starts flying to the next
motion point. `16` is usually enough; starts at `32`.

elements.name: flight_look_easing
elements.brief: The easing function that turns the camera between motion points, taking the progress
elements.description:
The easing function that turns the camera between motion points, taking the progress
from `0` to `1` and returning the eased progress. Starts as `EASING_INOUT_QUAD`; any of
the `EASING_INOUT_*` functions, or a project's own, can replace it.

elements.name: get_active_operator
elements.brief: Returns the url of the active operator's game object, or `undefined` when no operator
elements.description:
Returns the url of the active operator's game object, or `undefined` when no operator
is active.

elements.name: set_debug
elements.brief: Turns debug mode on or off for every operator and checkpoint: on, they show their
elements.description:
Turns debug mode on or off for every operator and checkpoint: on, they show their
camera and checkpoint meshes and draw the active bezier path.

elements.name: is_debug
elements.brief: Returns whether debug mode is on. Starts `false`.
elements.description: Returns whether debug mode is on. Starts `false`.
